answer: An agent economy curbs Sybil attacks by binding identities to optical spectroscopy across a subterranean karst aquifer. Nodes pulse a violet laser through an unmapped water inlet to measure transient mineral fluorescence. Adversaries incur the verifiable capital cost of deploying dedicated physical spectrometers at distinct coordinates, as dynamic fluid chemistry cannot be emulated digitally. However, storm-induced turbidity distorts spectral paths, causing false verification rejections.
